review.decision: Approve before test or product edits
review.notes: The final selection must agree with the originally selected record, fresh live occupants and batch claims on both routes. Observe current pane ID, locator and shell immediately before a compatibility write. The directory control keeps the actual post-start assertion and existing bound.

cases.description: A queued historical guess still has one available owner at dispatch
cases.setup: Two renamed panes have distinct historical owners in a private home. A log-only tmux and isolated sender handle every command.
cases.action: While the first item starts, add a second eligible record, restore the original live shell locator, or make the conversation live elsewhere. Compare with unchanged ownership.
cases.expected: The stable second target receives its literal and Enter once. Each changed case issues neither and records a changed target.

cases.description: A compatible launcher writes only into the same live shell target
cases.setup: Two targets share a private restore batch. The second explicitly selects a compatibility wrapper.
cases.action: During the first dispatch leave the second shell stable, switch it to an editor, change its locator, or make the target query fail. Inspect every sender call and terminal receipt.
cases.expected: The stable target receives the wrapper command and Enter. Changed or unreadable targets receive neither and report target-changed.

cases.description: Detached session directory assertions observe completed child startup
cases.setup: Use a private HOME and explicit private tmux socket. Keep the original directory, detached, identity and replay assertions.
cases.action: Observe a real child with its requested directory, with a single inherited-directory observation, and with a permanently incorrect observation. Apply the same bounded check to root-home and remote creation.
cases.expected: A transient observation can settle at the exact requested directory; a permanent mismatch still fails at the existing 5-second bound. No production timeout or directory logic changes.
